comments.author: @WorldTravelDocumentary18
comments.text: The DR Congo has incredible natural wealth, yet so many people still struggle to survive. To me, the real tragedy is not a lack of resources, but who actually benefits from them. Do you think Congo will ever turn its riches into a better life for its people?

comments.author: @travelintolifeus
comments.text: What stays with me is the contrast between the beauty of the Congo rainforest, the incredible wildlife, and the struggles people face every day. As an American, I think we sometimes forget how much a country's wealth underground means nothing if ordinary people cannot share in its benefits. The Congolese people deserve to see a brighter future.

comments.author: @AmazingDiscoveriesTopUS
comments.text: The Leopard's return to the 2026 World Cup brought joy after 52 years, but the US currently advises against travel because of an Ebola outbreak and instability in the east.

comments.author: @UnseenOutlands
comments.text: The Congo River is fascinating, especially knowing how deep and powerful parts of it are. But I'm curious about the people living along its banks. Does the river make transportation and trade easier for remote villages, or do dangerous currents and seasonal changes create serious challenges?
